notes:
CIRCUIT: five inverting op-amp stages (all five have their feedback element from the top-left '-' input to the apex output, and their bottom-left '+' input strapped to GND -- except A2/#3, whose '+' input is driven from the centre node). Sources: 5V V-DC (#6) top-left, 10A I-DC (#18) bottom-left. 24 components, 12 nets.

NET MAP
  0  = ground rail: GND #7 #8 #15 #17 #22 #23, V-DC #6 bottom lead, I-DC #18 bottom lead, and the '+' inputs of A1(#2), A4(#10), A3(#14), A5(#19).
  n1 = V-DC #6 top lead + left plate of C1(#0) + '-' input of A1(#2); the y~190 rail from x=140 to the op-amp, dotted at (218,191).
  n2 = right plate of C1(#0) + output of A1(#2) + left end of R1(#5); the y~235 wire from the apex to x=408 and on to the resistor.
  n3 = right end of R1(#5) + left end of L1(#1) + '-' input of A2(#3); the y~245 wire, dotted at (556,242).
  n4 = right end of L1(#1) + output of A2(#3) + left end of R2(#4); the y~270 wire, T at (750,270).
  n5 = the big centre node at the solder dot (422,543): '+' input of A2(#3) via the staircase up to (555,285), right end of L2(#13), output of A3(#14) via the x=323 stub, left end of R3(#11), left plate of C3(#20) via the x=421 column down to y~780.
  n6 = the right-hand rail x~915 from y~270 to y~800: right end of R2(#4), right end of R4(#12), right end of R5(#21). Three terminals, no other load -- odd but that is what is drawn.
  n7 = right plate of C2(#9) + output of A4(#10) + left end of R4(#12); the y~592 wire, T at (765,593).
  n8 = right end of R3(#11) + left plate of C2(#9) + '-' input of A4(#10); the y~548 wire, dotted at (594,546).
  n9 = I-DC #18 top lead + left end of L2(#13) + '-' input of A3(#14); the y~600 wire from x=50 to x=205, T at (152,601).
  n10 = right plate of C3(#20) + left end of L3(#16) + '-' input of A5(#19); the y~775 wire, dotted at (549,774).
  n11 = right end of L3(#16) + output of A5(#19) + left end of R5(#21); the y~801 wire, T at (715,801).

SITE DECISIONS (all CRITICAL sites explicitly ruled junction; none needed overriding, but each was read at pixel level):
  S6 (218,191) junction - fat symmetric solder blob, T-shape: the C1 feedback column drops onto the V-DC/A1-input rail. Crossing here would strand C1's left plate on a one-terminal net and leave A1 with no feedback.
  S12 (408,233) junction - T: the C1 right-plate column ends on the A1 output wire. Crossing would leave C1's right plate dangling.
  S13 (556,242) junction - T with slight thickening: L1 left column drops onto the R1->A2 input wire. Crossing would remove A2's feedback and strand L1.
  S16 (750,270) junction - T: L1 right column ends on the A2 output wire. Same argument.
  S27 (422,543) junction - 4-way with an unmistakable round solder dot ~3x stroke width in both axes (dot score 2.7). The tracer also reported hop=5.7 here, which is spurious: the crop shows no arc and no jog, just a dot with four straight branches. Reading it as a crossing would split A3's output/R3/C3 from A2's '+' input and leave the y=543 rail and the x=421 column as separate nets, which contradicts the dot.
  S28 (594,546) junction - T: C2 left-plate column drops onto the R3->A4 input wire.
  S29 (323,548) junction - T: the A3 output stub rises from y=635 and ends on the L2/centre rail. Crossing is not even geometrically possible (only three branches, one of them a stub).
  S34 (911,588) junction - T: R4's right lead ends on the right-hand vertical rail. Crossing would leave R4's right terminal on a one-terminal net.
  S36 (152,601) junction - T: L2's left column drops onto the I-DC/A3-input wire. Crossing would remove A3's feedback.
  Non-critical sites S0-S2, S7-S9, S11, S15, S17-S21, S30, S31, S35, S39-S42, S44, S47-S49 are handwriting ('1MF', '1MH', '1NH', '1KOhm', '5V', '10A') or symbol ink brushing a wire, or T-joins inside a net that is already correct; defaults left alone.

PORT / PIN FIXES
  #0 Capacitor t1: tracer had it on p2@(332,157), a stroke of the '1MF' label under the box (net n2 had one terminal). Moved to p0@(352,125), the real right plate lead (wire length 168).
  #6 V-DC t1: tracer had it on p1@(151,275), a stroke of the '5V' label (net n8 had one terminal). Moved to p2@(138,274), the real bottom lead running to GND #8.
  #18 I-DC t1: tracer had it on p1@(98,732), a stroke of the '0' in '10A' (net n15 had one terminal). Moved to p2@(55,755), the real bottom lead to GND #22.
  #14 Op-Amp t1: tracer had it on p2@(289,564), stray '1NH' ink (net n12 had one terminal). Reassigned as part of the pin reorder below.
  Op-amp pin order (required in+, in-, out). All four triangles are drawn with '-' on the upper-left lead, '+' on the lower-left lead, output at the right apex; the tracer's default order was wrong on every one of the five:
    #2  -> t0=p2(269,244)='+', t1=p0(268,197)='-', t2=p1(381,233)=out
    #3  -> t0=p0(581,284)='+', t1=p2(581,244)='-', t2=p1(701,269)=out
    #10 -> t0=p4(640,603)='+', t1=p1(640,548)='-', t2=p2(761,594)=out   (p0/p3 at (761,520)/(759,511) are the C2 feedback column brushing the box corner, not leads)
    #14 -> t0=p3(175,648)='+', t1=p1(175,599)='-', t2=p0(288,628)=out
    #19 -> t0=p2(582,828)='+', t1=p0(582,774)='-', t2=p1(695,804)=out
  Each fix is confirmed by the '+'/'-' glyphs being legible inside every triangle and by the resulting negative-feedback path (C1 on A1, L1 on A2, L2 on A3, C2 on A4, L3 on A5).

CLASSES: no reclassification needed; every symbol matches its label (2 plates = Capacitor, coils = Inductor, zigzag = Resistor, circle with +/- = V-DC, circle with arrow = I-DC, triangle = Op-Amp, hatch = GND).

UNRESOLVED: none. The only oddity is n6, a three-resistor node with nothing else on it (the three stage outputs are tied together through 1k each and go nowhere else); the ink is unambiguous -- the right-hand rail runs continuously from (915,270) to (915,800) with T-joins at y=270, y=588 and y=800 -- so it is recorded as drawn.
